REPAIR PASS. Previous trace left V-DC 2 (15 V) and I-DC 4 (10 A) with both terminals on '0'. Root cause: it assumed the bottom rail IS ground because column C runs down to GND 9. In fact column C's lower leg CROSSES the bottom rail at (262,452) and carries on to GND; the rail is a different node. Evidence at 1x greyscale: of the three column/bottom-rail meetings, columns B (x[176..196] y[444..460]) and D (x[340..360] y[450..468]) TERMINATE -- their verticals stop dead in the blob, no ink below y=455 / y=463 -- whereas column C (x[252..272] y[444..460]) passes straight THROUGH: ink continues at x=262-263 for y=455..482 and runs on into GND 9's bars (bbox centre (261.3,484.9)). So (262,452) is a 4-way crossing, not a T; the two real T's are marked identically (same small ring blob), so the ring is not a junction dot, and the standard rule (unmarked 4-way = crossover) plus circuit sense both give the crossover reading. The junction reading dead-shorts two of the five sources, which cannot be the intended netlist. 

Net map. Ladder of four vertical L-C branches (columns A..D left to right: 1uH+5uF, 5uH+10uF, 10uH+50uF, 50uH+100uF) hung between a top rail and a bottom rail, with the five sources stacked in column E (x~430). n1 = TOP RAIL (y~21): tops of Inductors 6, 7, 10, 8 and the top of V-AC 1. n2 = h2 (y~80-87): column A's mid-point (Inductor 6 bottom / Capacitor 5 top, junction dot at (85,85)) run right, HOPPING columns B (172,80), C (267,80) and D (352,79), to the junction dot at (434,87) between V-AC 1 and I-AC 0. n3 = h3 (y~175-177): column B's mid-point (Inductor 7 bottom / Capacitor 11 top, junction dot at (181,177)) run right, hopping columns C (263,177) and D (349,175), to the dot at (429,174) between I-AC 0 and V-DC 3. n4 = column C's mid segment only: Inductor 10 bottom + Capacitor 13 top. h4 hops it -- the col-C vertical loops out to x=252 across y=258..272 and returns (greyscale x[244..276] y[253..280]), the same left-loop glyph this drafter uses at every verified crossover. n5 = column D's mid segment only: Inductor 8 bottom + Capacitor 12 top; h5 hops it, the col-D vertical looping out to x=341 across y=351..371. n6 = BOTTOM RAIL (y~452-460; continuous x=76..430 apart from 1-3 px pen skips) TOGETHER WITH column B's lower leg and h4. Column B runs unbroken from Capacitor 11's bottom plate (y=239) down through h4's T at (181,262) to its termination dot on the rail at (185,452), so h4 -- which hops column C at (261,262) and column D and lands between V-DC 3 and I-DC 4 -- is on the rail node. n6 therefore = {Capacitor 5 bottom, Capacitor 11 bottom, Capacitor 12 bottom, V-DC 3 bottom, I-DC 4 top, V-DC 2 bottom}. 0 = COLUMN C's LOWER LEG + h5 + GND 9: from Capacitor 13's bottom plate (y=327) down through h5's T at (261,358), across the bottom rail at (262,452) WITHOUT joining it, to GND 9. h5's left end is a clean T there (vertical straight through, blob at y=356-365, horizontal leaving right from x=269) and h5 hops column D at (353,357) before landing between I-DC 4 and V-DC 2. So 0 = {Capacitor 13 bottom, GND 9, I-DC 4 bottom, V-DC 2 top}. 

Judgment calls: (a) THE decisive one is (262,452), argued above. (b) Consequence: V-DC 2 and I-DC 4 sit in PARALLEL between n6 and 0 in opposite orientations -- the same textbook motif already recorded for this drafter in circuit_87 and in the companion sheet circuit_153 (which is this identical circuit drawn transposed, and whose GND lead likewise crosses a rail). (c) The three column/rail markers all look like small open rings at low zoom; at 1x they are 6-7 px ink blobs with a 1-2 px pen void. The void is NOT the discriminator -- topology is: B and D terminate, C passes through. (d) Every mid-rung crossing on this sheet is the drafter's left-loop detour in the VERTICAL, verified at 1x: h2 x B/C/D, h3 x C/D, h4 x C, h5 x D. No horizontal is ever interrupted. (e) 2-terminal parts are listed top-then-bottom as drawn; V-DC 3 and V-DC 2 both have '+' on top, I-AC 0 and I-DC 4 both point up. Order does not affect any metric. (f) Nothing is off-frame: every bbox centre lies inside 512x512. (g) Remaining Tier-2 finding: Inductor 6 sits in parallel with V-AC 1 (both n1-n2), i.e. a source/inductor loop that is singular at DC. That is inherent to this drawing -- the top rail is the source-stack top AND every inductor's top -- and is a genuine AC-textbook property, not a trace error.
